What it means for you

One change. Three conversations.

For coordinators

Spend more time solving problems

The agent extracts details and drafts tickets. You check, approve, follow up and handle exceptions. Meridian committed to no job losses during the pilot. Your supervisor will arrange practice and coaching.

Bring a concern to your huddle
For clients

Clearer updates and a familiar contact

Keep using the usual service desk channel. The coordinator reviews the ticket and approves dispatch. For an urgent issue or feedback on an update, reach your account manager or the duty coordinator.

See your feedback route
For leaders

Expand in stages and check the results

The Head of Service Desk owns quality, response time and the authority to pause. Review the scorecard and customer feedback before releasing each group of sites.

Review the rollout gates

Rollout and safeguards

Start small. Expand after review.

  1. Day 30 · 2 sites

    Draft and review

    Coordinators review every draft and report missing details, confusing prompts and extra work.

  2. Day 60 · 10 sites

    Check the quality

    Review handling time, first-pass accuracy, rework and complaints weekly before expanding.

  3. Day 90 · board review

    Expand in waves

    Meridian’s worked case expands to 30 sites. Keep the same human approval rules and publish progress in the monthly review.

Human approvals and a stop rule. Agents use authorised records and record their actions. Coordinators approve dispatch. The Head of Service Desk pauses the pilot if rework exceeds 20% for two consecutive weeks.

Help improve the transition

Tell us what needs to change.

Describe the step that caused friction, the impact and one change to try. Leave out tenant details and use your established channel.

Staff

Bring the issue to your supervisor or team huddle. Ask for a practice session when a task or approval is unclear.

Clients

Use your usual service desk or account manager. Ask the duty coordinator for help with an urgent issue.

Leaders

Take recurring concerns to the weekly service desk review. Assign an owner, test the fix and report back in the monthly update.
